fact: Mali's customs directorate reports that offices continued to be switched into production on SYDONIAWorld in 2017-2018, with the international transit module and a direct-removal procedure in operation.
Mali's Director-General of Customs said the move to SYDONIAWorld in 2015 built an integrated system that now covers over 95 percent of customs business procedures.

Douanes Ivoiriennes report that Cote d Ivoire and Mali teams met on 24-25 September 2026 to assess SIGMAT in its operating phase on the Abidjan-Bamako transit corridor, sharing information between the two administrations.
The UN Global Survey 2025 round records Mali's automated customs system as fully implemented.
The Togolese Revenue Office announced the pilot phase of the interconnection of the Togo and Mali customs systems via Burkina Faso on the Lome-Bamako corridor, operational from 10 March 2025.

Customs directors general of the Sahel Confederation (AES) states and Togo reviewed in Lome the interconnection of their customs IT systems, under instruments signed at Niamey on 23 July 2024 that set the legal framework for it.
ECOWAS says Mali was connected to the SIGMAT goods-in-transit data exchange system in July 2024, though it also lists Mali among states preparing to put it into operation.
